data.name: Actin cytoskeleton
data.description: Cell shape and motility machinery. The original TOR2 phenotype in yeast, and the mammalian mTORC2 function that showed the second complex is acutely rapamycin-insensitive (JAC2004, SAR2004); the two-complex model itself came from biochemistry (LOE2002).
data.description_beginner: The scaffolding that gives a cell its shape and lets it move. It was one of the first jobs pinned on mTORC2 - first in yeast, then in mammalian cells - and one that rapamycin does not block in the short term. The idea of two separate mTOR complexes itself came from purifying the proteins.

reading_levels.student: mTORC2-dependent actin organisation and cell shape control.
reading_levels.research: The original TORC2 phenotype in yeast; in mammals mediated through PKCα and Rho GTPases and largely rapamycin-insensitive acutely.

studies.title: mTORC2 controls actin polymerization required for consolidation of long-term memory
studies.authors: Huang W; Zhu PJ; Zhang S; Zhou H; Stoica L; Galiano M; Krnjevic K; Roman G; Costa-Mattioli M

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Conditional Rictor-knockout mice (postnatal forebrain) and Drosophila
studies.finding: Conditional deletion of Rictor in the postnatal mouse forebrain reduced mTORC2 activity and selectively impaired long-term memory and the late phase of hippocampal LTP, with a comparable long-term-memory deficit in dTORC2-deficient flies. Hippocampal actin polymerisation was reduced, and restoring it rescued both L-LTP and long-term memory; a compound that raised mTORC2 activity converted early LTP into late LTP and enhanced memory. This is the loss-of-function AND rescue evidence that mTORC2 is required for memory consolidation - the arm chronic rapamycin also disrupts, and the study Open Question H8 needs for its mTORC2 liability leg, which until 2026-09-05 rested on no supporting study at all.

relations.mechanism: One of the first functions assigned to mTORC2 was shaping the cell's skeleton. In yeast it was the original TOR2 phenotype; in mammalian cells it showed that the second complex is acutely rapamycin-insensitive.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC2's first known job was shaping the cell's internal skeleton. It was found in yeast first, as the original TOR2 phenotype, and then in mammalian cells - where it stood out precisely because rapamycin didn't block it.
relations.boundary: Mammalian cells, yeast, Drosophila and conditional Rictor-knockout mice (JAC2004, SAR2004, LOE2002, HUA2013). The cytoskeleton phenotype was defined in cell lines and yeast; its role in intact tissue is less tested.
relations.note: The two-complex model itself came from biochemistry (LOE2002, JAC2004, SAR2004).
